workflow_metadata.name: Functional Analysis Workflow
workflow_metadata.description: Analyze and decompose functions and their interactions - focuses on WHAT functions exist and HOW they interact (NOT which service implements which function)
workflow_metadata.purpose: Standalone functional architecture analysis - define and validate functional decomposition before service allocation
workflow_metadata.key_distinction: This workflow focuses on FUNCTIONAL ARCHITECTURE (what functions, how they interact). Service architecture workflows (01b/01c) focus on SERVICE ALLOCATION (which service implements which function).
workflow_metadata.when_to_use: When you want to focus on functional decomposition and analysis without immediately committing to service boundaries. Can stop here for architecture-only deliverables, or continue to service architecture.

NOT_required.00b-framework_selection: NOT needed - framework selection is for system architecture (services/components), not functional architecture. Functional architecture is framework-agnostic and always creates a DAG.

standard.description: Standard functional analysis entry - new system functional decomposition

from_feature_update.description: Functional analysis for feature update - analyze delta to existing functional architecture

workflow_steps.name: Functional Requirements Extraction
workflow_steps.description: Extract and document functional requirements from foundational documents

actions.purpose: Understand WHAT the system must do at highest level

actions.method: Parse mission statement and user scenarios to identify required capabilities
outputs: List of functional requirements (FR-001, FR-002, etc.)

actions.purpose: Ensure all user scenarios covered by functional requirements
validation_criteria: All success criteria traceable to requirements

workflow_steps.name: Functional Flow Definition
workflow_steps.description: Define functional flows showing process sequences, decisions, and data flows

actions.description: Identify functional flows from user scenarios
actions.method: Map each user scenario to process flows
Break down each flow into discrete, reusable functions

function_definition.function_type: read | write | process | decide | generate | validate | iterate

actions.method: Map which functions call which other functions
dependency_types: data_flow (Function A outputs data that Function B consumes)
control_flow (Function A completion triggers Function B)
error_flow (Function A error triggers Function B error handler)
actions.creates_dag: Yes - function dependency graph is a directed acyclic graph (DAG)

actions.note: This is a MACHINE-READABLE specification for analysis

gates.name: Functional Architecture Defined
checks: All user scenarios mapped to functional flows
All flows decomposed into atomic functions

workflow_steps.name: Functional Architecture Visualization
workflow_steps.description: Generate human-readable visualizations of functional architecture for stakeholder validation
workflow_steps.rationale: CRITICAL: Stakeholders cannot validate machine-readable JSON - must create visual diagrams using standard notation (BPMN, UML)

actions.purpose: Show sequence of functional operations using BPMN 2.0 notation
Show branching logic and conditions using decision tree notation
Show data movement and transformation using UML notation
Show which functions call which other functions
Generate markdown documentation describing functional architecture

gates.name: Visualizations Generated
checks: All 4 diagram types created (process, decision, data, dependencies)

workflow_steps.name: Stakeholder Validation
workflow_steps.description: Review functional architecture visualizations with stakeholders to validate completeness and correctness
workflow_steps.rationale: Stakeholder sign-off on functional architecture BEFORE service allocation prevents costly rework and misalignment

review_questions: Do the functional flows accurately represent how the system should work?
Are there missing functions needed to support user scenarios?
Are there unnecessary functions that don't add value?
Do the decision points cover all necessary conditions?
Does the functional architecture align with expectations?

actions.description: Obtain stakeholder sign-off or identify refinements needed
outcomes: APPROVED: Stakeholders validate functional architecture - proceed to FA-05
REFINEMENTS NEEDED: Critical issues identified - return to FA-02 or FA-03 to address

gates.name: Stakeholder Validation
gates.note: MANDATORY gate - cannot proceed to technical analysis without stakeholder validation

workflow_steps.name: Technical Analysis & Gap Detection
workflow_steps.description: Analyze functional architecture for technical issues: gaps, redundancies, inefficiencies, context bottlenecks

actions.purpose: Convert functional architecture to graph representation for NetworkX analysis

analyses: Unreachable functions (functions not reachable from entry points)
Dead-end functions (functions with no outgoing edges)
Missing error handlers (functions without error handling paths)
Incomplete flows (user scenarios not fully covered by functions)
Unnecessary functions (functions not contributing to user scenarios)
High fan-out (functions calling too many others)
High fan-in (functions called by too many others - potential bottleneck)

actions.description: Run context bottleneck analysis (AI workflows only)
actions.condition: Only if system is an AI agent workflow with context consumption tracking
analyses: Context consumption paths (cumulative token consumption along paths)
Context bottlenecks (paths exceeding available context window)
actions.purpose: Ensure AI agents can complete workflows within their context windows

severity_levels.CRITICAL: Gaps, unreachable functions, or context bottlenecks that will prevent system from working - MUST FIX
severity_levels.WARNING: Redundancies or inefficiencies that should be addressed - SHOULD FIX

workflow_steps.name: Iterative Refinement
workflow_steps.description: Refine functional architecture to address critical issues from stakeholder feedback AND technical analysis
workflow_steps.rationale: Dual validation (stakeholder + technical) ensures functional architecture is both correct AND complete

actions.description: Review all issues from stakeholder feedback (FA-04) and technical analysis (FA-05)
Prioritize issues by severity and impact
priority_order: 1. CRITICAL technical issues (gaps, unreachable functions, context bottlenecks)
2. CRITICAL stakeholder issues (missing functions, incorrect flows)
4. WARNING stakeholder issues (scope concerns, minor misalignments)

actions.description: Automated gap closure proposals (OPTIONAL but RECOMMENDED)
actions.purpose: Automatically propose solutions for functional gaps using chain_reflow matrix analysis and architecture linking
actions.when_to_use: When CRITICAL gaps are detected in FA-06-A02
outputs: specs/functional/gap_closure_report.json (proposed functions and connections to close gaps)

gap_closure_strategies.unreachable_functions: Use matrix_gap_detection.py: Given current functions (State A) and required outputs (State C), solve for connector functions (State B) to bridge gaps
gap_closure_strategies.dead_end_functions: Propose output handlers or downstream functions
gap_closure_strategies.incomplete_flows: Use matrix analysis to find missing intermediate functions in user scenario paths
gap_closure_strategies.orphaned_functions: Use link_architectures.py to discover connections to existing functions

actions.review_required: YES - LLM must review proposed functions before accepting. Gap closure tool proposes solutions but does not automatically modify functional_architecture.json
actions.time_savings: 5-30 minutes per gap (automated proposals vs manual gap analysis)

actions.description: Refine functional architecture to address critical issues (MANUAL or using gap closure proposals from FA-06-A02B)
refinement_actions: Review gap closure proposals from FA-06-A02B (if generated)
Add missing functions identified by stakeholders, gap analysis, or automated proposals
Remove redundant functions identified by redundancy analysis
Refactor inefficient flows identified by efficiency analysis
Correct flow sequences based on stakeholder feedback
Add missing decision branches or error handlers
actions.note: Can use gap_closure_report.json as input for automated proposals

actions.returns_to: FA-03 actions (generate all diagrams and documentation)
FA-04 actions (stakeholder review of refined visualizations)
FA-05 actions (regenerate graph, re-run gap/redundancy/efficiency analysis)

actions.condition: Loop continues if CRITICAL issues remain from EITHER stakeholder validation OR technical analysis
termination_criteria: No CRITICAL stakeholder issues (stakeholder sign-off obtained)
No CRITICAL technical issues (no gaps, unreachable functions, or context bottlenecks)

loop_structure.exit_condition: No critical issues from stakeholder OR technical validation
loop_structure.max_iterations: No hard limit - iterate until quality achieved

gates.name: Functional Architecture Validated (Dual Validation)
checks: No CRITICAL stakeholder issues (stakeholder approval obtained)
No CRITICAL technical issues (gap/redundancy/efficiency analysis passes)
No missing functions (100% user scenario coverage)
gates.success_message: Functional architecture validated by BOTH stakeholders AND technical analysis

workflow_steps.name: Functional Architecture Finalization
workflow_steps.description: Finalize functional architecture deliverables and prepare for next phase (service allocation or architecture-only deliverables)

actions.description: User decision: Continue to service allocation or stop here?
options: OPTION A: Continue to service architecture - run 01b-bottom_up_integration or 01c-top_down_design to allocate functions to services
OPTION B: Stop here (architecture-only deliverables) - functional architecture is complete and validated
actions.if_option_a: Proceed to service allocation workflow (01b or 01c) - functional architecture will guide service boundaries
actions.if_option_b: Workflow complete - deliver functional architecture package to stakeholders

gates.name: Functional Architecture Package Complete
checks: User decision made (continue to service allocation or stop)

workflow_steps.next_step: COMPLETE (or 01b/01c if user chooses to continue to service allocation)

gates.name: Functional Architecture Validated (Dual Validation)
gates.critical: BOTH stakeholder AND technical validation must pass

quality_gates.enforcement: All gates blocking - cannot skip steps

next_workflow.routing_note: User decides in FA-07-A04 whether to continue to service allocation or stop here

required: Functional flows defined and functions decomposed (FA-02)
Technical analysis complete with no critical issues (FA-05)

success_criteria.functional_completeness: 100% user scenario coverage by functional flows and functions
success_criteria.stakeholder_alignment: Stakeholder sign-off obtained - functional architecture matches expectations
success_criteria.technical_correctness: No critical gaps, redundancies, or inefficiencies - architecture is sound
success_criteria.context_feasibility: No context bottlenecks (for AI workflows) - workflows completable by AI agents
success_criteria.deliverables_complete: All 8 functional architecture artifacts created and validated

critical_reminders: This workflow focuses on FUNCTIONAL ARCHITECTURE (what functions, how they interact) - NOT service allocation
Stakeholder validation (FA-04) is MANDATORY - must obtain sign-off on visualizations before technical analysis
Dual validation required: BOTH stakeholder (FA-04) AND technical (FA-05) must pass
Iterative refinement (FA-06) is a LOOP - continue until no critical issues from EITHER source
User decides at FA-07 whether to continue to service allocation (01b/01c) or stop here
Use existing tools: system_of_systems_graph_v2.py with --functional-mode flag
Visualizations use standard notation: BPMN for processes, UML for data flows
llm_agent_guidance.key_distinction: Functional architecture = WHAT + HOW functions interact. Service architecture = WHICH service implements WHICH function. This workflow handles the former, 01b/01c handle the latter.
when_to_use_this_workflow: User wants to focus on functional decomposition before committing to service boundaries
User wants architecture-only deliverables without implementation
User wants to validate functional design with stakeholders before technical allocation
User wants to analyze functional completeness and efficiency before building
